about.title: Hollister Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: Patients in Hollister trust local providers with some of the most important decisions of their lives, from surgeries to diagnoses to ongoing treatment. Most of the time, care goes as expected. But when a provider deviates from the accepted standard of care and a patient is harmed, California law gives injured patients a path forward — one that comes with strict rules and short deadlines. Because San Benito County residents often travel to nearby counties for specialized treatment, malpractice claims here can involve multiple providers and jurisdictions, adding complexity. LawProactive doesn't practice law or promise any result; we simply connect you, free of charge, with an independent attorney in our network who can review your medical records, explain your realistic options, and help you understand whether what happened meets California's legal standard for malpractice. There's no obligation to move forward after that conversation.

whyChoose.title: What Hollister Patients Should Know About California's Rules

items.title: Strict, Short Deadlines
items.desc: California generally requires a malpractice claim within one year of discovering the harm, and never more than three years from the injury itself. Missing this window can end a claim regardless of its merits, so early review matters.

items.title: 90-Day Notice Requirement
items.desc: Before filing suit, California law requires giving the healthcare provider 90 days' written notice of the intent to sue. An attorney can help make sure this step is handled correctly and on time.

items.title: Expert Review Is Almost Always Needed
items.desc: A bad medical outcome by itself isn't proof of malpractice — California requires a qualified medical expert to establish that the standard of care was breached. Independent attorneys in our network work with the right resources to evaluate this early.

items.question: How long do I have to bring a medical malpractice claim in Hollister?
items.answer: California generally requires filing within one year of discovering the injury, and no later than three years from when it occurred, whichever comes first. There are limited exceptions, so it's worth having your timeline reviewed promptly. Waiting can seriously limit your options.

items.question: Does a poor outcome from surgery automatically mean malpractice?
items.answer: No — California law recognizes that medicine carries inherent risks, and a bad result alone isn't enough to prove malpractice. A claim generally requires showing the provider deviated from the accepted standard of care and that this deviation caused harm. This is why a qualified medical expert typically has to review the case.

items.question: Are there local hospitals or clinics in Hollister connected to these claims?
items.answer: Hollister residents receive care through local providers as well as facilities in surrounding San Benito County and nearby areas, and claims can sometimes involve more than one provider or location. An independent attorney can help sort out where and against whom a claim may need to be filed. LawProactive can connect you with someone who handles these details.

items.question: What does LawProactive charge for connecting me with an attorney?
items.answer: Nothing — our connection service is completely free to injured patients. Attorneys in our network generally work on contingency, meaning there's no fee unless you recover compensation. This lets you get informed about your options without upfront cost.
